items.statement: Raw milk prices increased 8.9% YoY; market milk prices increased 4.9% (INR2.67/liter). Value-added product prices increased 6.6% (weighted average INR75/liter vs INR70.40). Ghee prices increased ~15%.
items.quote: For the quarter that went by, which is Q3, our raw milk -- while the raw milk prices increased by about 8.9%, the market milk prices on a weighted average basis across our regions, we have been able to increase by about 4.9%.

items.statement: Procurement costs rose sharply due to industry-wide butter tightness and attractive global dairy trade prices leading to butter exports. December weighted average milk procurement price was INR46.01/liter vs quarterly average INR45.57/liter
items.quote: The month ending cost of milk price in the month of December was -- weighted average price was INR46.01. So, if it gives you a sense of how sequentially that has increased because for the quarter, the reported number that we have put is about INR45.57.

items.statement: YTD milk procurement volumes declined 0.82% to 16.86 lakh liters/day for 9M FY26. Q3 procurement averaged 16.73 lakh liters/day, down 9% YoY. Bulk butter inventory minimal at 390 tonnes (<1 month cover).
items.quote: For the first time in several years, YTD milk procurement volumes declined marginally by 0.82% to 16.86 lakh liters per day for 9 months of FY '26, following three consecutive years of 9% to 10% year -on-year growth. Q3 procurement averaged 16.73 lakh liters per day, down 9% year-on-year, reflecting milk shortages.

items.statement: Hyderabad ice cream plant trial production underway; commercial commissioning expected in current quarter (Q4 FY26). Flavored milk plant also expected to be commissioned in current quarter.
items.quote: The Hyderabad ice cream plant is progressing as planned with trial production underway now and commercial commissioning expected in current quarter. The flavored milk plant is also expected to be commissioned in the current quarter, positioning the company well to capture incremental demand across fast-growing categories.

items.statement: Ice cream plant first-year capacity utilization expected at 40-45%. Ice cream business grew 21% YoY in Q3, up from 16-17% in Q2. Paneer grew ~30% YoY; capex for paneer capacity planned for Q2/Q3 FY27.
items.quote: In the first year of operation, we expect a capacity utilization of about 40% to 45%. 40% is what we are expecting, and this is on -- as per business plan. We don't expect any surprises unless the summer goes bad and ice cream business is impacted.

items.statement: Value-added product revenues grew 22.6% YoY, contributing 38% of total revenue vs 33.8% last year. Ghee and butter consumer packs included. Curd growth slowed to ~10% (vs usual 13-14%); drinkables grew 16%; paneer grew ~30%.
items.quote: Including ghee and butter consumer packs, value -added product revenues grew 22.6% year -on-year, contributing 38% of total revenue compared to 33.8% in the corresponding period last year, underscoring sustained premiumization and mix improvement.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin in 7-9% range (not formal guidance). Current consolidated EBITDA ~6.2%, standalone ~5.4%. Expect margins to progressively normalize with improving supply, higher VAP contribution, and disciplined execution.
items.quote: We would like to keep our EBITDA towards the 7 to 9 percentage range, which means that at this point in time, which I feel is the lowest point we would have hit, we're still about 0.7, 0.9 percentage below that level.

items.statement: Logistics cost as % of revenue increased from 2.7% to 2.9% (0.2pp impact). Marketing spend increased from 1.2% to 1.8% of revenue (0.6pp impact) as conscious investment ahead of summer season.
items.quote: The other expense, which has gone up is our marketing investments this year in quarter 3 of this year compared to quarter 3 of previous year has gone up by about 0.5%. Last year, Q3 was about 1.2 percentage of revenue. This year, Q3 is about 1.8 percentage of revenue.

items.statement: One-time provision for defined benefit obligations under Ind AS 19 due to new labor codes: INR27.42 million standalone, INR27.78 million consolidated, recognized as employee benefit expense.
items.value: INR27.42 million standalone; INR27.78 million consolidated
items.quote: Following the notification of new labor codes, the company recognized a onetime increase in provision for defined benefit obligations under Ind AS 19, that is Employee Benefits, resulting in an incremental provision of INR27.42 million on a stand -alone basis and INR27.78 million on a consolidated basis during the quarter.

items.statement: Organized trade contributing 18-19% of sales with higher uptick, stickiness, and retention. E-commerce platforms showing significantly improving brand stickiness. New high-protein products (Nourish+ paneer 60g protein, Nourish+ milk) launch
items.quote: Organized trade is already contributing about 18%, 19 percentage of our sales. And we are seeing a higher uptick, higher stickiness, higher retention rate for our brands in these channels, thanks to these marketing efforts.

items.quote: I'm also pleased to share that Mrs. Brahmani Nara, Executive Director, was honored at the Business Today, most Powerful Women in Business Awards 2025 and Mrs. Nara Bhuvaneswari, Vice Chairperson, Managing Director, received the Outstanding Dairy Professional Award 2025 from the Indian Dairy Association.

items.quote: Nothing meaningful yet. At the end of the day, InstaHelp caters to a more high -frequency daily/ weekly cleaning and housekeeping service. And our core consumer services business, to the extent that there is some overlap, it is in deep cleaning.

items.statement: Consolidated break-even targeted by Q3 FY28; adjusted EBITDA of ~1,000 crores targeted by FY31
items.quote: we have a high degree of confidence, let me put it that way, on both those numbers that we have put down, which is Q3 F28 break even on a consolidated basis and 1000 crores of adjusted EBITDA by FY31.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA marginally ahead of FY25 (previously guided flat); sustained margin improvement from FY27 onwards
items.quote: FY26 in the previous earnings call, we had said will be flat over FY25, but we've seen slightly better performance than we had expected. And therefore, we've upgraded to saying FY26 will also be marginally ahead of FY25.

items.statement: Core India Consumer Services (ex-InstaHelp) to see steady adjusted EBITDA margin improvement year-on-year from FY27
items.quote: FY27 onwards, we should see sustained adjusted EBITDA margin improvement in India Consumer Services, ex of Insta. That's where we have maximum certainty.

items.statement: International business (UAE, Singapore) sustainably broken even; margin expansion expected year-on-year, 1.5-2 years behind India in margin maturity
items.quote: Second place where we have high certainty now is in our international business in UAE and Singapore. We've been a bit conservative in the projections there, because their business is still early. But we believe that business is also broken even sustainably.

items.statement: Native expected to break even and contribute meaningfully to FY31 EBITDA target, but timing and quantum uncertain
items.quote: We do believe in the foreseeable future Native will break even and it will meaningfully contribute to that 1000 crores adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: InstaHelp losses to peak around Q3 FY28 then decline; break-even targeted by FY31 at the latest
items.quote: we believe at some point around that period, InstaHelp losses might peak and then start to come down. And if that assumption is to play out, then as InstaHelp losses, the growth driver of that consol adjusted EBITDA going from sort of call it 0 to 1000 is a function of already elevated adjusted EBITDA for the core businesses, continuing to compound and InstaHelp losses coming down and eventually b

items.statement: India Consumer Services (ex-InstaHelp) aims to grow at 2x market rate (market growing 10-11%); driven by new user acquisition, coverage expansion, and better proposition
items.quote: we internally definitely the ambition to grow this business at at-least 2x of what the market is growing at.

items.statement: InstaHelp ordering frequency an order of magnitude higher than core services, but AOVs an order of magnitude lower; steady-state frequency unclear
items.quote: InstaHelp's ordering frequency is definitely an order of magnitude better than the India consumer services business. Of course, the AOVs are an order of magnitude lower.

items.statement: Cross-pollination occurring between InstaHelp and core services users; encouraging enough to continue investing in InstaHelp
items.quote: we're definitely seeing it happen, and it is encouraging enough for us to continue to invest behind InstaHelp.

items.statement: Core India services moving toward instantaneous delivery (within hour/half-hour) in high-density micro markets; densification drives profitability
items.quote: whether it's beauty services, whether it's electricians, plumbers, carpenters, AC repair, bathroom cleaning, etc., all of those services, we are pushing hard to make them more and more instantaneous.

items.statement: InstaHelp target AOV 1.8-2x current ~172 rupees (net order value) for break-even; requires 80-90% reduction in customer discounting and improved partner utilization
items.quote: So in InstaHelp, we believe that AOVs need to be about 1.8 to 2x where they are today in that range, in steady state for this business to essentially break even.

items.statement: InstaHelp worker can do 3-5 orders/day at ~1.5 hours each; target healthy partner earnings via utilization, not earning support
items.quote: a typical order in InstaHelp category where you're calling for a house help worker might be one to two hours, averaging about one and a half hours or so. So an InstaHelp worker, if well utilized, can comfortably do between three to five orders in a day.

items.statement: No meaningful incremental investment needed to make core services instantaneous; densification improves partner utilization and micro-market profitability
items.quote: We don't think incremental investment as such is needed to move that towards instantaneous behavior. In fact, on the contrary, as we flip micro markets, quote unquote, towards becoming more instantaneous in nature, partner utilization actually improves.

items.statement: InstaHelp hero geography expected to emerge in 2-3 quarters; top priority metros: Gurgaon/Delhi NCR, Bangalore, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune
items.quote: over the next two, three quarters, I think there'll be one of these markets which will emerge as a hero market for us where the metrics, etc, are all aligning well in terms of profitability, maturity of the micro markets, our own market leadership being cemented.

items.statement: Social security provisions for employees/contract workers largely one-time (new wage definition, leave encashment); gig worker contribution details awaited
items.quote: some of the amounts are actually one -time in nature because we had to take into account the new definition of wages as well as look at, you know, leave encashment balances for employees and contract workers specifically.

items.statement: Fixed cost dip Q-o-Q attributed to operating rhythm and seasonality (marketing spend 25 to 13 crores); business best evaluated year-on-year
items.quote: If you see, you know, Table 4B, where we disclose the P&L for the India consumer services business, you will see a dip in the marketing expenses from 25 crores to 13 crores, you know, between contribution profit and adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: No consideration of acquisitions for InstaHelp; fully focused on organic build
items.quote: Right now, we are just fully sharply focused on building organically. We have our hands full with serving our customers and service partners. It is not even a thought that has occurred in my head.

items.statement: International like-to-like growth ~79% Y-o-Y (ex-Saudi JV impact); UAE and Singapore markets structurally similar to India, growing profitably
items.quote: if I remove the impact of that and look at like-to-like growth, like -to-like growth in this quarter has been about 79%. So very healthy.

items.statement: Customer retention 'smile graph' driven by cross-category adoption; post-COVID cohorts larger but less pronounced smile vs pre-COVID early adopters
items.quote: customers, A, getting retained well in the same category and over time, also trying out newer categories as they get confidence and trust on the platform. And consequently, customer retention across categories and lifetime value increases.

items.statement: All branded purifier filters now reported under Native segment; not a recent change
items.quote: Basically, Devanshu, any branded filters that we sell on our platform are also Native brand only. So all of them get reported under the Native segment.
